This page explains, in plain language and without code, what this study chose and why. The general background it relies on is on [Methodological background](methodological_background.qmd). The formal specification is the [analysis plan](analysis-plan.qmd); each section below ends by linking the part of the plan that governs it. Three kinds of note mark where the description stands:

- **Specified in:** the section of the analysis plan that defines the method.
- **Current code:** where the code does not yet do what the plan says, what it does now, with a link to the GitHub issue tracking the difference.
- **Decision pending:** a choice the plan has not yet made, linked to its decision issue. A paragraph that starts with **Decision pending:** is highlighted in yellow automatically.

## The question and the design in brief

This study uses the national transplant registry to compare outcomes after kidney–pancreas and pancreas-alone transplantation between recipients with and without HIV. Because recipients with HIV may differ from others in their donors and their own characteristics, each recipient with HIV is compared with similar recipients without HIV rather than with everyone. Kidney–pancreas and pancreas-alone transplants are studied separately, because their risks differ.

The comparison is planned, not yet carried out, and it describes how outcomes differ between similar recipients with and without HIV. Whether HIV itself causes any difference depends on assumptions the data cannot fully check (see [Comparing similar recipients](#comparing-similar-recipients) below).

**Specified in:** [§1 Objective](analysis-plan.qmd#1-objective) and [§2 Design](analysis-plan.qmd#2-design).

**Decision pending:** which outcome is primary ([#7](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/HIV-pancreas-2024-srtr/issues/7)).

## Who is included

Recipients aged 16 or older at transplant who received a kidney–pancreas or pancreas-alone transplant. Four exclusions are applied in order, each shown as a step in the flow diagram: no transplant date recorded; age under 16; no patient status date recorded; and a pancreas donor risk index (PDRI) that cannot be calculated. The PDRI is a summary of donated-pancreas quality, and it needs every one of its inputs, including how long the pancreas was preserved before transplant. So the rule for missing preservation time decides who is excluded at the last step.

Recipients are counted as having HIV if the registry records a positive HIV test at transplant.

**Specified in:** [§4 Study population](analysis-plan.qmd#4-study-population) and [§5 Exposure and time zero](analysis-plan.qmd#5-exposure-and-time-zero).

**Decision pending:** how missing preservation time is handled, which sets who is excluded for a missing PDRI ([#10](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/HIV-pancreas-2024-srtr/issues/10)).

**Decision pending:** how recipients whose HIV status is missing or unknown are classified ([#9](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/HIV-pancreas-2024-srtr/issues/9)).

## Comparing similar recipients

Two methods are planned, both built on a propensity score: each recipient's estimated chance of having HIV, given the quality of the donated pancreas (the PDRI), the year of transplant, the cause of diabetes, and the recipient's age, sex and race.

- **Matching:** each recipient with HIV is paired with up to ten recipients without HIV who have similar scores.
- **Weighting:** every recipient without HIV is kept but weighted, so that together they resemble the recipients with HIV.

Both aim to make the groups alike in the characteristics that went into the score. Neither can balance characteristics the registry does not record, such as HIV control (viral load and CD4 count) or how centers chose recipients. Any difference that remains can still reflect those, not HIV alone.

**Specified in:** [§6 Comparator or matching](analysis-plan.qmd#6-comparator-or-matching).

**Decision pending:** how close the matched groups must be before the comparison goes ahead ([#12](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/HIV-pancreas-2024-srtr/issues/12)).

**Decision pending:** which characteristics go into the weighting, and whether weighting is a main or a supporting analysis ([#21](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/HIV-pancreas-2024-srtr/issues/21)).

## What is compared

Six outcomes are followed from the day of transplant:

- **Graft loss:** the transplanted organ stops working, for example a pancreas that no longer controls blood sugar, or a kidney that leaves the recipient needing dialysis. Kidney graft loss applies only to kidney–pancreas recipients; pancreas graft loss applies to both groups.
- **Treated rejection:** an episode of the immune system attacking the organ that was treated with anti-rejection medicines. Rejection can be reversed and is not the same as graft loss, though it can lead to it. Kidney rejection applies only to kidney–pancreas recipients.
- **Death** from any cause.
- **Cancer** reported on a follow-up form.

For each outcome, follow-up stops at a censoring point, and how death and graft loss are handled is still open. Graft loss could be counted only while the recipient is alive (death treated as the end of follow-up), counted regardless of death, or analysed with death as a competing outcome. Similar choices apply to rejection and cancer after graft loss or death. Until that decision is made, the outcome labels in the plan describe the intended measures, not a settled method.

**Specified in:** [§7 Outcomes](analysis-plan.qmd#7-outcomes) and [§8 Statistical analysis](analysis-plan.qmd#8-statistical-analysis).

**Decision pending:** when follow-up stops for each outcome, and whether death is treated as the end of follow-up or as a competing outcome ([#13](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/HIV-pancreas-2024-srtr/issues/13)).
